key: Ask what the structure does: sperm-transport structures (the SEED) and the ureteric bud come from the mesonephric duct, while the tubes, uterus, cervix and upper vagina come from the paramesonephric duct.
items: Testosterone keeps the upper mesonephric duct, which coils into the epididymis next to the testis.
The mesonephric duct below the epididymis becomes the thick-walled vas deferens that carries sperm to the urethra.
The seminal vesicle buds from the caudal mesonephric duct and supplies fructose-rich alkaline fluid to semen.
The terminal mesonephric duct beyond the seminal vesicle becomes the ejaculatory duct, which opens into the prostatic urethra.
The ureteric bud sprouts from the mesonephric duct in both sexes, which is why duct and kidney anomalies travel together.
In females the mesonephric duct regresses, and a surviving remnant in the lateral vaginal wall forms a Gartner duct cyst.
The unfused upper parts of the paramesonephric ducts become the fallopian tubes.
The fused caudal paramesonephric ducts form the uterovaginal canal, whose upper part becomes the body of the uterus.
The cervix forms from the fused lower paramesonephric ducts, so complete fusion failure duplicates it in didelphys.
The fused paramesonephric ducts form the upper vagina, which meets the urogenital sinus part at the vaginal plate.
In males anti-Müllerian hormone removes the paramesonephric duct, leaving only a small cranial remnant on the testis.
Uterine septum that fails to resorb
A persistent wall between the fused paramesonephric ducts leaves a septate uterus, the most common Müllerian anomaly.
